title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were deployed into a predictable high-traffic scenario without adequate preparation for it. On the Fourth of July, multiple vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets as their batteries drained during heavy congestion from fireworks celebrations and unplanned road closures. The system was not designed to handle the traffic volume and disruptions that occurred, leaving vehicles immobilized without human drivers present.

This shows a gap between the operating conditions a system was built for and the real-world scenario it was sent into. The vehicles lacked sufficient battery capacity or routing logic to navigate extended periods of gridlock, and there was no failsafe to prevent passengers from being stranded or to clear vehicles from traffic flows. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, adding a secondary failure mode.

Whether the traffic conditions were truly unforeseeable, or whether Waymo should have anticipated the impacts of a major holiday on San Francisco's streets, is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on Saturday following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations. Videos verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up stationary on streets, with some requiring towing after their batteries drained during heavy traffic. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. Passengers and other motorists expressed frustration at the gridlocked vehicles with no drivers present.

Waymo stated its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles and said the company is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic disruptions. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to hold conversations with public and private partners about the incident to ensure smoother traffic management for future events. This incident follows a December power outage when some Waymo vehicles stopped at intersections with nonworking traffic lights.
